title: COPE Ethical Guidelines for Peer Reviewers (COPE Council, Version 2, September 2017)

extracted.subtask_short: Substantiating a reviewer's own claim-evidence critique
extracted.subtask_description: Sets ethical standards for how a peer reviewer must substantiate their own assertions about a manuscript's claims and evidence, including distinguishing evidence essential to support claims from merely-desirable additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantiate general statements with specific supporting evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Be specific in your critique, and provide supporting evidence with appropriate references to substantiate general statements, to help editors in their evaluation.' A reviewer asserting that a claim is unsupported is itself expected to substantiate that assertion with specifics (line numbers, contradicting citations, etc.), not merely assert disbelief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation must be congruent with report content
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Ensure your comments and recommendations for the editor are consistent with your report for the authors.' Any accept/revise/reject recommendation should be congruent with the comments provided in the review - a reviewer cannot privately flag an unsupported claim while publicly endorsing the paper's conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish evidence essential to support claims from merely strengthening additions
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Be clear which (if any) suggested additional investigations are essential to support claims made in the manuscript under consideration and which will just strengthen or extend the work.' An explicit instruction to distinguish 'this evidence is required to justify what you are claiming' from 'this would be a nice addition.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not the job of the reviewer to extend the work beyond its current scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation suggestions must be substantively justified, not self-interested
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should refrain from suggesting authors include citations to their (or an associate's) work merely to increase citation counts or enhance visibility of their or an associate's work; suggestions must be based on valid academic or technological reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to underlying data required before verifying claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should understand the scope of review expected before starting (e.g., whether review of raw data is expected), getting back to the journal if anything is not clear and requesting any missing or incomplete items needed - verifying claims may require access to underlying data, and reviewers should ask for it if it is missing.
